## Why This Benchmark Is Included

Standard Transformer encoder classification task.

| **Field** | **Value** |
|:---|:---|
| **Classroom value** | Demonstrates tokenization, padding, attention, and fine-tuning. |
| **Systems behavior** | Encoder attention, dynamic sequence lengths, and batch padding. |
| **Benchmark lineage** | Published DistilBERT checkpoint evaluated on GLUE SST-2. |
| **Model choice** | Official compact checkpoint has a published accuracy baseline. |
| **Dataset choice** | SST-2 is the checkpoint's named evaluation task. |
| **Quality metric** | Accuracy is the standard SST-2 metric. |
| **Published baseline** | 0.9105504587155964 verified accuracy in the pinned Hugging Face model-index metadata |
| **Alternative rejected** | A custom micro-BERT has no equivalent upstream quality contract. |

## How to Run

```bash
# one-time asset preparation
uv run mlperf fetch --workload text-classification --profile max

# benchmark run (writes JSON/HTML/CSV reports + .provd.json provenance)
uv run mlperf run --workload text-classification --profile max

# quick smoke pass
uv run mlperf run --workload text-classification --profile min

# research envelope
uv run mlperf run --workload text-classification --profile pro
```

See the [running guide](../../guide/running.qmd) for profile semantics, report handling, and power measurement flags.

## Systems Experiment Execution Contract

**Within-run measurement protocol:**

| **Field** | **Value** |
|:---|:---|
| **Primary metric** | inference_seconds |
| **Scenario** | offline |
| **Timing scope** | five repetitions of the full 872-example SST-2 validation split after tokenized inputs and model weights are resident on the selected device |
| **Included phases** | batched PyTorch model execution |
| **Excluded phases** | model and dataset fetching, model construction, tokenization and host-to-device transfer, one untimed warmup for each observed batch shape, accuracy computation, report and provenance serialization |
| **Device synchronization** | synchronize immediately before and after the measured inference region |
| **Outer reference runs** | 1 |
| **Outer preconditioning runs** | 0 |
| **Outer inter execution cooldown seconds** | 5 |
| **Repeatability metric** | inference_seconds |
| **Repeatability limit** | 0.05 |

## Results

To make the metric concrete, one run of this benchmark on Apple M5 Max observed `accuracy` of 0.9106, taking 4.3311 `inference_seconds`.

That is an illustration, not a target and not a score. It comes from a single machine and your hardware will produce different timing. The number that matters is the one your own run reports.

Run the benchmark and read your own report:

```bash
uv run mlperf run --workload text-classification --profile max
```

Every run writes an HTML dashboard for reading, JSON for machine use, CSV for spreadsheets, and a `.provd.json` provenance manifest. Those artifacts carry the quality decision, timing distribution, hardware and software fingerprint, asset digests, and model lineage for the run you performed.

See [Reading Results](../../guide/results.qmd) for how to interpret them.
